# About this script

This script shows the workflow for evaluating Mean Pairwise Distance (MPD) using the last step corrected traits. It follows the same pipeline as the raw trait one, or: 

1) Computes multi-trait Gower distances using corrected trait data of terrestrial ferns from the Southern Atlantic Forest (SAF).

2) Calculates Standardized Effect Size of Mean Pairwise Distance (SES.MPD) under both abundance-weighted and presence/absence frameworks.

3) Fits linear models to evaluate relationships between SES.MPD and environmental drivers.

4) Tests model residuals for spatial structure using Moran's I and Spatial Eigenvector Maps (MEM).

5) Evaluates model robustness against sampling effort using Cook's distance correlations.

The results of this script will be part of Table 2, Appendix S12 and Appendix S14.

> ![WARNING] 
> Run this script demands a lot of memory (\~4 GB) and take a minute to end. Therefore, clear garbage accumulated with `gc()`, the environment and restart the session. You may not be able to run this script if you have less the 8 GB of RAM memory.

# Packages and setup

As usual, multiple packages are required to do run this script, most of them are available on CRAN. Some then isn't available CRAN, see below.

```{r}
# .rs.restartR() ## Restart R session
rm(list = ls())  # Clear all objects from the environment
gc()  # Run garbage collection to free up memory

library(patchwork)
library(SYNCSA)
library(vegan)
library(readxl)
library(here)
source(here("func/cwm_sig.txt"))
source(here("func/summarize_trees.R"))
library(openxlsx)
library(tidyverse)
library(foreach)
library(doParallel)
library(gawdis)
library(bbmle)
library(jtools)

set.seed(811)  # Set seed for reproducibility
options(scipen = 9999)  # Disable scientific notation in outputs
N <- 1000  # Number of simulations or iterations (e.g., number of trees)
runs <- 999  # Number of permutations (if needed)
```

# Load data 

In this step we will load the organized data, with the original values `org_all` alongside with `scomp`, i.e., phylogenetic corrected trait for the 1,000 scenarios.

```{r}
org_all <- readRDS(here("data/org_data.RDS"))  # Load original data
scomp <- readRDS(here("outputs/RDS/SCOMP.RDS"))  # Load simulated trait components

```
# Do Parallel Computing

As in others scripts we will use parallel computing to hurry to work with the lists and hurry up the process.

```{r}
no_cores <- detectCores() - 6  # Detect available cores, reserve 5 for system
registerDoParallel(cores = no_cores)  # Register parallel backend
cl <- makeCluster(no_cores, type = "FORK")  # Create cluster for parallel tasks
```
# Organize data

We will iteratively structure data with SYNCSA, combining traits and environment.

```{r}
org_data <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% {
  organize.syncsa(
    org_all$community,
    traits = data.frame(
      diam = scomp$riz_diam[[i]],
      rcomp = scomp$riz_comp[[i]],
      r_cr = scomp$riz_cr[[i]],
      r_lr = scomp$riz_lr[[i]],
      lmseg = scomp$lam_mseg[[i]],
      buds = scomp$buds[[i]],
      ltri = scomp$ltri[[i]],
      ind = scomp$ind[[i]],
      lmorf = scomp$lmorf[[i]],
      chl = scomp$chl[[i]]
    ),
    envir = org_all$environmental
  )
}
```

# Elaborating Gower Distance Matrix

As in the raw trait script we will calculate the functional diversity to our data based on a Gower distance matrix, divided into 3 groups (i.e., 1-competition, 2-protection and 3-reproduction). This method reduces discrepancies in the correlation of individual-trait and multi-trait matrices [(de Bello et al. 2021)](www.doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13537).

```{r}
# Compute Gower distance matrix between trait values, considering trait groups
all <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% {
  gawdis(
    org_data[[i]]$traits,
    groups = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 3, 3),  # Define trait groupings
    silent = TRUE
  ) %>% as.matrix()
}
```

# SES Mean Pairwise Distance weighted by species abundance (absolute frequency)

Calculate Standardized Effect Size of MPD incorporating species abundances under a richness null model.

After, we will select the best model for each trait, as following:
1) Creating a list of models names (see Appendix S1 for the hypothesis of each model);
2) Elaborating the linear models, based on the list;
3) Iteratively select the most parsimonious models based on AICc;
4) Iteratively filter only the best model (dAICc = 0);
5) Save in a new object for summarize in a table.

```{r}
# Compute standardized effect sizes (SES) of MPD for each iteration
ses.mpd_all <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% {
  picante::ses.mpd(
    org_data[[i]]$community,
    all[[i]],
    abundance.weighted = TRUE,  # Use species abundances
    null.model = "richness"  # Null model maintains species richness
  )
}

```

## List of candidate linear models for MPD (see Appendix S6)

## Selecting models based on AICc

```{r}
# Compare all models using AICc and retain best-fitting model
sel_md <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    AICctab(
      m1[[i]],
      m2[[i]],
      m3[[i]],
      m4[[i]],
      m5[[i]],
      m6[[i]],
      m7[[i]],
      m8[[i]],
      m9[[i]],
      m10[[i]],
      m11[[i]],
      m12[[i]],
      m13[[i]],
      m14[[i]],
      m15[[i]],
      m16[[i]],
      base = T,
      delta = T,
      mnames = models
    ) %>%
      `class<-`("data.frame")
  }
```
## Filtering results for just the best model (delta=0)

```{r}
# Keep only models with ΔAICc = 0 (best models)
result_1 <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    cbind.data.frame(
      models = rownames(sel_md[[i]]),
      sel_md[[i]],
      row.names = NULL
    ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(dAICc == 0)
  } %>%
  plyr::ldply(.fun = data.frame)
head(result_1)
```

## Running models again to keep the coefficients

```{r}
mods <- foreach(i = 1:N) %do%
  {
    lm(formula = result_1$models[i], data = org_data[[i]]$environmental)
  } 
 

# Extract model coefficients and summary statistics
result <- map_dfr(mods, get_model, mpd = T)
result_ses.all <- result

# Calculate mean ± SD of coefficient
mod_ses.all.df <- result %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      .cols = everything(),
      .fns = function(x) {
        paste0(round(mean(x, na.rm = T),3),"[", round(sd(x, na.rm=T),3), "]")
      }
      )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(nsel= tapply(result$model, result$model, length), .before = 2)

sel_md_ab <- m13
mod_ses.all.df
glimpse(mod_ses.all.df)
```
# Plotting MPD correlation with richness

```{r}
# Correlation between MPD and species richness
a <- map_dfr(ses.mpd_all, function(x) {
  a <- cor.test(x$ntaxa, x$mpd.obs)$estimate
  b <- cor.test(x$ntaxa, x$mpd.obs)$p.value
  cbind.data.frame(cor = a, p = b)
})

a %>%
  apply(MARGIN = 2, function(x) {
    rbind(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
  })

# Save scatter plot to TIFF
tiff(
  file = here('figs/mpd_tcor.tiff'),
  width = 180,
  height = 130,
  units = "mm",
  res = 300
)
plot(
  y = ses.mpd_all[[1]]$ntaxa,
  x = ses.mpd_all[[1]]$mpd.obs,
  col = "black",
  bg = alpha("lightgreen", .7),
  cex = 2,
  pch = 21,
  xlab = "Mean Pairwise Distance All Traits (Corrected)",
  ylab = "Species Richness",
  family = "serif",
  alpha = .5
)
text(
  x = 0.1,
  y = 22,
  "Frequency Weighted \n Mean Pearson's r = 0.52 [± 0.02]\n P-value = 0.05 [± 0.003]",
  family = "serif"
)
dev.off()
```

# Spatial correlation

## Abundance-weighted SES

```{r}
# Load spatial analysis packages
library(adespatial)
library(DHARMa)
library(SoDA)
library(sp)
library(spdep)

# Function to mensure Moran's I based on @Bauman2018 proceed
test_mem <- function(res, lw, nmodel = NULL) {
  mem <- mem.select(res, lw, method = "MIR", nperm = 999, p.adjust = T)
  sac <- data.frame(
    I = mem$global.test$obs,
    Pvalue = mem$global.test$pvalue
  ) %>%
    mutate(model = nmodel, .before = I) %>%
    `rownames<-`(NULL)
  if (length(mem) > 1) {
    message('Check MEM data for eigenvectors...')
    mem_data <- list(
      sac = sac,
      selected.MEM = mem$MEM.select,
      summary = mem$summary
    )
    return(mem_data)
  } else {
    message('No MEM selected...')
    return(sac)
  }
}

#Filter env data based on the rows of ses.mpd matrix
all_df <- org_data[[1]]$environmental %>%
  dplyr::filter(rownames(.) %in% rownames(ses.mpd_all[[1]]))

## Creating a cartesian coordinates df, which will permit Euclidean distance usage
df_xy <- SoDA::geoXY(
  latitude = all_df$Lat,
  longitude = all_df$Long,
  unit = 1000
)
dim(df_xy)
dist <- dist(df_xy)


# Create a spatial weighted matrix
nb <- chooseCN(coordinates(df_xy), type = 4, plot.nb = FALSE)
distnb <- nbdists(nb, df_xy)
fdist <- lapply(distnb, function(x) 1 - x / max(dist(df_xy)))
lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = 'B', glist = fdist, zero.policy = TRUE)

# Create model
model <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    ses.mpd_all[[i]]$mpd.obs.z ~
      org_data[[i]]$environmental$max_temp_wam *
        org_data[[i]]$environmental$prec_warm +
        org_data[[i]]$environmental$samp_size +
        org_data[[i]]$environmental$plot_size
  )

#Extract residuals
res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

# Mensure Moran's I
ab_moran <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  test_mem(
    res[[i]],
    lw,
    nmodel = 'SES_MPD_AB ~ Max. Temperature * Rainfall Warmest Month'
  )

# Combine results in a DF
ab_cor_df <- list_rbind(ab_moran)
```

## Presence/absence SES.MPD

```{r}
model <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    ses.mpd_pa[[i]]$mpd.obs.z ~
        org_data[[i]]$environmental$nitrogen +
        org_data[[i]]$environmental$samp_size +
        org_data[[i]]$environmental$plot_size
  )

res <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% residuals(model[[i]])

pa_moran <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  test_mem(
    res[[i]],
    lw,
    nmodel = 'SES_MPD_PA ~ Nitrogen'
  )
pa_cor_df <- list_rbind(pa_moran)
```

## Save data 

```{r}
# Function to compute mean and sd of coefficients (p-value and I)
resume <- function(x){sapply(x, function(col) {
  if(is.numeric(col)){
      mean_1 <- mean(col, na.rm = TRUE)
      sd_1 <- sd(col, na.rm = TRUE)
      paste0(round(mean_1, 3), " [±", round(sd_1, 3), "]")} else{
    unique(col)
  }
})
}

ab <- resume(ab_cor_df) # applying to the frequency weighted model
pa <- resume (pa_cor_df) # applying to the presence/absence model

# Save in xlsx
write.xlsx(
  x = list(ab = ab_cor_df, pa = pa_cor_df, resume = rbind(ab, pa)),
  file = here('outputs/ses_corrected_correlation.xlsx')
)
```

# Model Robustness and Cook's Distance Diagnostics
Here we follow the same principles as before, but we do it using mean Cook's Distance for each site across the 1,000 scenarios. The results will be a supplement for Table 2, Appendix S12 and Appendix S14.

```{r}
str(org_data[[1]])
org_data[[1]]$environmental

cook <- sapply(sel_md_ab, function (x) { 
        cooks.distance(x)
}) %>% rowMeans(.) 

org_all$environmental$mean_cook_ab <- cook[match(rownames(org_all$environmental), names(cook))]


cook_2 <- sapply(sel_md_pa, function (x) { 
        cooks.distance(x)
}) %>% rowMeans(.) 

org_all$environmental$mean_cook_pa <- cook_2[match(rownames(org_all$environmental), names(cook_2))]

CS_ab <- cor.test(org_all$environmental$mean_cook_ab, log10(org_all$environmental$samp_size), method = "kendall") %>% tidy() %>%
        mutate(model = "Abundance", .before = 1)

CS_pa <- cor.test(org_all$environmental$mean_cook_pa, log10(org_all$environmental$samp_size), method = "kendall") %>% tidy() %>%
        mutate(model = "Presence", .before = 1)

CS_sum <- rbind(CS_ab, CS_pa)

# Saving correlation
write.xlsx(CS_sum, file = here("outputs/CS_cor_CSES.xlsx"))

# Plotting association of richness and cooks distance
tiff(filename = here("figs/cook_ses_cor.tiff"), width = 180, height = 100, units = "mm", res = 300)
par(mfrow = c(1,2),  mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
plot(y = org_all$environmental$mean_cook_ab,
     x=log10(org_all$environmental$samp_size),
     cex.main = 0.8,
     cex.lab = .7,
     cex.sub = .6,
     cex.axis = .6,
     pch = 15,
     col=rgb(0,0,0,0.5),
     sub = "Kendall: 0.23; P = 0.09",
     main = "SES.MPD Abundance Weighted (Corrected)",
     ylab = "Coefs. Cook's distance",
     xlab = "Sample size (m² - log10)",
        ylim = c(0,2))
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "red")

plot(y = org_all$environmental$mean_cook_pa,
     x=log10(org_all$environmental$samp_size),
     cex.main = 0.8,
     cex.lab = .7,
     cex.sub = .6,
     cex.axis = .6,
     pch = 15,
     col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5),
     sub = "Kendall: 0.01; P = 0.92",
     main = "SES.MPD Presence/Absence (Corrected)",
     ylab = "Coefs. Cook's distance",
     xlab = "Sample size (m² - log10)", ylim = c(0, 2))
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "red")
dev.off()
```
